summary:
The headline signal today is bullpen's rise across the board — R1, R2, and R3 all show bullpen at 54% over the last 14 days (102-88, n=190) with a 3-game winning streak on all three ratings, up from a season baseline in the 51% range. That's the category to lean on, and it lines up nicely with SEA @ MIL, the day's strongest consensus play where all four ratings stack MIL with deltas up to +2.49 on R4. MIL is also a proven team-when-liked spot at 25-15 (62%, n=40) with strong plays going 14-8 for +4.0u, so this is about as clean a green light as the model offers today. Contrast that with SP, which is ice cold on R3 (47%, -5.0pts flagged COLD) and sitting at just 46% over 14 days on R1 and R2 too — meaning any game where the projected delta is being driven mainly by starting pitching split deserves a discount. TOR @ TBR is worth flagging here: Bieber vs. Seymour is a real SP-driven storyline, but TBR still grades as a team-when-liked stud (25-10, 71%, strong 18-5 for +22.0u), so the bullpen/trends combo should be doing the heavy lifting on that pick, not the arms.

On the cold side, STL @ CIN is the day's biggest fade — all four ratings agree STL is the play but by wide negative deltas (down to -2.19 on R4), essentially the mirror image of the MIL game and worth treating as a legitimate CIN lean if the model's directional consensus is this strong. NYY @ BAL and WSN @ TEX are milder versions of the same pattern, both drawing full four-rating agreement toward the "away trending down" side. Category-combo-wise, trends+runs remains the best agreement pair at 55.7% (236-188, n=424), and trends is red-hot everywhere (54% across all three live ratings, n=190) — any today's-slate pick where trends and bullpen both point the same direction, like MIL or TBR, should carry more weight than one where only SP or hitting is doing the pointing. Bankroll-wise, respect R1's rough 7-day stretch on strong plays (-7.0u, 46%) versus R3's better 30-day form (+19.0u, 52%) when sizing bets that lean on those specific ratings today.
